steps.text: This is as far as we can go, Your Imperial Majesty.
You are the only one in all of Yan who may enter the room beyond this door.
It is but a door. There is no need to be so fearful.
It conceals Yan's greatest secret, and its greatest asset, Your Imperial Majesty...
...Is that so?
The seventeen-year-old True Lung walks down the last few steps.
He looks back at the three Grand Ministers behind him, who are still bowing deeply. He frowns and pushes the door open.
He has heard about what lies behind the door. The legends and stories of this ancient nation that have been passed down through the centuries—
'The Earth's blessings have granted this stone to its people; the Heaven's blessings shall bring an end to Sui.'
Some say that the prosperity of Yan comes from it. Others say the True Lung's authority is merely borrowed from it.
But no one has seen it with their own eyes in nearly a century.
The ascending True Lung is filled with excitement, his fingertips trembling.
Everything in the land of Yan shall obey him, for the prosperity of Yan—
...So will one small crystal.
He pushes the door open.
As ambitious as he is, he could not help but stop before the massive space and blinding light.
It is not the first Originium itself, but man-made additions upon it, the limiters and guidance that generations after generations of Tianshis have placed upon it over the centuries.

a.text: At the new capital of Baizao, a tomb was built to hold the vessel of Sui, and the consciousness of Sui was suppressed by the power of calamity. Yet the Emperor was not at ease, and so he sought counsel from the Tianshi Bureaus in hopes of keeping the peace for eternity hence.

Then the Emperor discovered the means to harness the power of calamity, but it would take the lives of a hundred Tianshis and ten thousand soldiers to form the blade and slay the beast. Even if complete success were achieved, Baizao would not be spared.
And the Emperor said, 'It is shameful to bring harm to the people for one's own purposes. I shall give up myself, and my descendants shall do the same, and not demand the sacrifice of the people.'
The True Lung passed the next year, and by it the enchantment was complete. The crown prince grieved and named it 'Bu Fan'.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: ...Bu Fan,  'No Rebellion'. Sounds like 'No Return' too.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: My ancestor sacrificed himself and made the reigning True Lung the subject of future human sacrifice. Henceforth, the True Lungs that came after him gave their lives to harness the power of this Originium.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I would not have known it was so massive if I did not see it for myself...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Yet it's no more than a tiny crystal compared to all of Yan and Yan's future.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Yan could have done much more with this object.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: How much energy have we spent on suppressing the sleeping beast? With such energy, how many armies could we have raised, how many machines could we have built?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: How could I tolerate such... inaction?
The True Lung lingers before the facility for a while. He has gotten used to the scorching light, and even starts to feel... boring.
A smile comes to his face as he remembers the reverence on his three Grand Ministers' faces. How will he deride their timidity when he leaves the room without being rude?
He recalls the 'rule' that kept the ministers out, for him to face this structure alone.
The rule that inextricably links it to his life.
He could not help but laugh.
The True Lung's authority over all under heaven, tied to a tiny crystal like this?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I am still inexperienced. I will be relying on the three of you for many things.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Yan has been peaceful and prosperous for centuries. Why is it that there are still rebellions?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Is there still land where the blessings of Yan do not touch? Or seditious subjects who will not submit to imperial rule?
Silence.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I will decide myself, then, as you do not answer.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: The blessings of Yan shall touch every corner, so that not a single person shall worry for food or shelter. The teachings for Yan shall reach every heart, so that not a single rebellious thought will enter the mind of a single man.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: We shall vanquish the northern traitors and build the nomadic city of Baizao. Both are the foremost priority, and neither shall be delayed.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: You shall summon the Six Ministries, discuss the specifics, and deliver a proposal by the end of the month.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Dismissed.
The trio on the other side of the curtain bow in assent and leave.
A little later...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Ah, you have arrived.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: ...It is an honor, Your Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I've long heard of the twelve 'extraordinary talents' of Yan, credited with no small number of achievements for the empire. I've been curious for some time.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I therefore perused the Sui Regulator's archives, and found something rather interesting.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Be it reports of triumph, or suspicious activities...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: No name has been mentioned more often than yours.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: But I see your visage is not as terrifying as the rumors claim.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: Why has Your Imperial Majesty summoned me?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: They call you the most cunning strategist in all Yan.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: How do you propose to resolve the two great obstacles we face?

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: The northern rebellion is hardly a major threat. The rebels may be influential in their local area, but they are powerless to expand. Nevertheless, it would be inadvisable to allow them to consolidate their position.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: Fifty-thousand soldiers and six months' worth of rations will be sufficient to defeat them.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Your estimate is much more optimistic than the Ministry of War... but I have more reason to trust your judgment on this.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: What about the other matter?

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: As for the modification of Baizao into a nomadic city... I understand the Ministry of Works has validated the engineering principles. The only issues are funding, supplies, and...

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: ...the Tomb of Sui beneath Baizao.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Yes. You understand the problem.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: It is for this that I have summoned you.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: How do you intend to eliminate Sui?

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: If you are familiar with the scrolls of the Sui Regulator... you understand that 'we' were the same and one as Sui, and our fates intermingled.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: Do you mean to ask how to kill 'us'?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: It is only 'Sui' that Yan is concerned about, and no other being.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: You understand, of course, the price that Yan paid for the hunt that occurred centuries ago.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: The price that must be paid, if Yan is to force the issue, is seven-tenths of its armies, one-tenth of its population, and fifty years of unceasing unrest.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: If that is the case, Yan will be in no position to ensure the safety of the twelve of you.
The proxy looks up and meets the gaze of the man behind the curtain.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I am determined to cleanse Yan of this thousand-year bane. I am not afraid to pay the price—any price.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: The Sui will be destroyed. The tremendous energy that was used to suppress that beast shall be reutilized to build a hundred cities and ten thousand battleships, and usher in another thousand years of prosperity for Yan.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I had hoped that there would be a place for the twelve of you in Yan's future prosperity, on account of your past deeds. It is regrettable.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: If your decision to eliminate Sui comes from practical judgment, rather than reckless pursuit of glory...

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: ...I may have a way.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: The twelve of us were one and same as Sui. We were destined to fade, whether It awakes or is destroyed.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: But it is possible that I could... replace It.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: How sure are you?

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: I will need time...
The young man behind the curtain points at the courtyard outside.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: That ginkgo sapling was planted in the spring of this year.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: The Ministry of Works swore an oath in this hall several days ago that the rebuilding of Baizao into a nomadic city will be complete before the tree bears fruit.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Twenty years. That is the time you have.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: That is too little time.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I am not here to bargain.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Immortality has made you arrogant. Perhaps you have forgotten that mortals do not have many 'twenty years'.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Yan cannot wait, and neither can I.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: You're the new Candleholder? So much time has passed, in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Has the previous Candleholder...

steps.name: Quiet Candleholder
steps.text: She retired last month, and asked me to tell you not to worry.

steps.name: Quiet Candleholder
steps.text: I will take over your communications with the Sui Regulator from now on.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Well, you'll have your hands full.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Most Candleholders have to worry about tracking down my free-roaming siblings. As for mine...

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: They have to sit in this office all day, handling books and scrolls. They are more like secretaries than Candleholders.

steps.name: Quiet Candleholder
steps.text: I enjoy reading and writing. This is right up my alley.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Perfect.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: What's your name?

steps.name: Quiet Candleholder
steps.text: I'm Chun.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: 'Chun'?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: 'For the ancient tree that shares your name, eight thousand years is a spring and eight thousand years is an autumn...' Was the one who named you remarkably ambitious, or remarkably cautious?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Wait, you are...?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: ...An Elf?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Judging from your appearance... you're an Elf of Yaan?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: The bestial Yaan and its Elves are well-versed in the ways of Yin-Yang and the Five Elements. The element associated with spring is wood, and the character for 'Chun' combines both 'wood' and 'spring', representing vitality and longevity... I see.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: My mother told me about it when I was young. I didn't expect anyone else to know.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Stuff like this is what history is about.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: It's your first day. I won't put you to too much hard work. Just familiarize yourself with the space; you can look at any books and documents in this study.
The Candleholder carefully scans the room. She could not conceal her eagerness as she sees scrolls and books that fill the wall shelves.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Did you write all of these?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: No, I simply collect the materials. The historians of the Imperial Historical Cabinet are the ones who actually write the books.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: After all...

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Is writing history a difficult task?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: It's a heavy responsibility.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: History books form people's perception of the past, but a few words are hardly enough to give them a complete view.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Choices must be made as to which parts to record for posterity, what sorts of lessons those who come after should learn...

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: It's easy to say, 'write with an impartial pen,' but it is a most profound and complex discipline.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: What if there is a mistake in the history books?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Then it should be corrected.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: History is inevitably warped by the position of the narrator, no matter how impartial the writer attempts to be.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I see a few more problems because I've lived longer than most and remember more than most.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Most... it's true that your kind, the proxies, are different from other long-lived. Before I joined, I heard that each of you had your own 'powers'.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Do you use your powers to correct the errors in the history books?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I heard you have a magical writing knife... do you use it to correct those errors?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: It can, but this is not how it should be used.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Mistakes take root in people's hearts as they are passed down from one generation to another. The proper way to fight them is to form a new consensus through debate and clarification, not to simply erase it.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Erasing a wrong word from one's own writing is not a significant issue, for it only concerns oneself.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: To do it to a published book would be to meddle with the memories of thousands.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: As for history... setting aside the question of how much I can alter, it will not be a good thing, for myself and for Yan.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Frankly, it's already a chore to ensure that history is not altered. I hardly have the energy to alter it myself.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Seems like there's something you would like to change with the knife yourself.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Huh?! I—

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Before my mother passed away, she said I may be the last of the Yaan Elves.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: She... she wanted me to find a home.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I wandered for many years. I tried many ways to blend in, but I always failed. Yan does not want—

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Yan does not want to accept you, because the Yaan Elves were depicted in the Great Hunt as... 'fickle and disloyal.'

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: But I know that's not true...

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The bestial Yaan stood against Yan simply to survive. That cannot be denied.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The Elves, though, had only wanted to mediate the conflict, yet they became the enemy of both sides... ultimately, most were killed in battle, and their deeds lost to time.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: So you wanted to alter this history?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I don't deny that I thought about it. But I'm your Candleholder now, and my work comes before all else.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I can't lend you the writing knife, nor can I allow you to use it to alter history.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I understand. I shouldn't have—

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: But if we can find proof that the Elves were in fact not disloyal, I will do all that I can to help you correct the erroneous records, in the proper manner.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Things haven't been too busy lately. We could visit the area where you used to live. What do you think?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I... I've only just come. Besides, the things I said aren't necessarily true. I—

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I can tell that your passion for words and history is genuine. Besides... who will believe you, if the historian does not?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Yes... yes!

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: This is the key to my office. You're my Candleholder now. Take good care of it.

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: How do you get in, if you give me the key?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Why should the master of the house need a key?

steps.name: Judicial Officer
steps.text: The court building has only just been completed! Why...?

steps.name: Ministry of Works Official
steps.text: Don't worry, it will not be torn down. Our Tumu Tianshis will transplant the Judicial Review Office to the nomadic plate, undamaged.

steps.name: Judicial Officer
steps.text: But wouldn't it have been so much cheaper to build it directly on the nomadic plate?

steps.name: Greedy Shopkeeper
steps.text: I hear the imperial court is putting everything behind this 'nomadic city'. I'm sure our cooperation will be very important.

steps.name: Tired Official
steps.text: Get to the point. What do you want?

steps.name: Greedy Shopkeeper
steps.text: My rosewood chair, ebony table, Kou-wu plates and Danyan lamps... none of them were inexpensive.

steps.name: Greedy Shopkeeper
steps.text: Here are the receipts from when I ordered my things. If there is any damage...

steps.name: Tired Official
steps.text: Fine, fine. You'll be reimbursed accordingly.

steps.name: Confused Guard
steps.text: Yes, the prisoners have been transferred.

steps.name: Confused Guard
steps.text: The previous instructions were from the Judicial Review Office, while the new ones are from the Ministry of Justice?

steps.name: Confused Guard
steps.text: I understand, but am I supposed to conjure the prisoners out of thin air?

steps.name: Confused Guard
steps.text: You don't care? The burdenbeast carriages are arriving in minutes?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Minister. Please excuse the poor hospitality. I did not know you were visiting.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I have never seen you in the Sky Mirror Pavilion. I take it you have important business?

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: There isn't much time, Miss Jie. I'll get straight to the point... there is an error in this year's archives that I would like to ask you to correct.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: A mistake in the documents that I audited? Pray tell.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: The documents submitted by the Ministry of Works state there were around a hundred deaths associated with the Chidao project at Danyan this year. Why did the number become three thousand?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: The figure of three thousand deaths was not cited from a single document, but calculated based on documents from the Ministry of Works, the Ministry of Revenue, and local government departments.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: The records are carefully sourced. I have kept a copy, should you wish to review them.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: While it is not my place to question the work of the Ministry of Works, I have no idea why the three thousand deaths in Danyan's local records became just a hundred when it reached Baizao.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: You must submit sufficient evidence, however, should you wish to question the documents audited by the Sky Mirror Pavilion.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: Ahem... well, Danyan is not so well-staffed as Baizao, and there are only limited resources available for record-keeping.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: Besides, the cold climate there causes disease and frostbite in winter. Perhaps not all of the three thousand died in the course of constructing the Chidao...

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I see. You wish for me to alter the documents to make the Ministry of Works look better before the cabinet.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: This is not about the cabinet. This is about Yan.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: You know about all the projects being carried out across Yan. They push the nation's resources to the limit, but there is no doubt that these projects will benefit the nation and its people.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: I'm not the only one who feels that such... depressing figures will weaken the people's morale.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I don't deny the benefits of these measures. Precisely because of that, the three thousand people who died to build the Chidao gave their lives for their country. It would be an insult to their memory to reduce it to a hundred.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Unless you can prove that there has been an error, any text that I have reviewed must not be altered. Anyone else who has a complaint can bring it to me directly.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: The nation must be united in the monumental task of building the nomadic city. Everyone at the court is doing their best, and each faces their own challenges...

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: Yet the writings of the Imperial Historical Cabinet and the Sky Mirror Pavilion have been most... aggressive and deprecating. It is as though you wish for work on the nomadic city to stop immediately!

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Is it the writer who has something to hide, or the reader?

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: How dare you...!

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: The imperial court has compensated the next of kin in full! Not a single coin has been withheld!

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I have noted this in the documents that I approved. The care that the imperial court has shown towards those injured and killed, as well as their families, illustrates Yan's love towards its people.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: Then why do you cling to a single number like this?!

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I understand your concern for Yan, minister. But I worry that people will only see the glory of the accomplishments, and not the people whose sacrifices made it possible.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: All I can do is to ensure that the history I see is recorded exactly as it is.

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: And you think you alone can decide the history of Yan?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: History has never been decided by one person. It is the combined soundless voices of millions.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: You are a learned man in a position to improve the lives of thousands upon thousands, minister. I simply leave behind some words for the people whose voices will never be heard.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Now, ask your conscience, and answer again for those people...

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: How many died building Danyan's Chidao this year? Was it a hundred... or three thousand?

steps.name: Minister of Works
steps.text: (Mutters irritably)

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: The Minister of Works just stormed off in a huff... is it because of Danyan?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Is this why you have come, sister?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I can't imagine how they managed to convince you to lobby on their behalf... am I actually dreaming, while the one in the Tomb of Sui has awakened?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Are you so sarcastic to everyone these days?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: I came to tell you that the Sui Regulator and the Ministry of Justice have approved your request to clear the Yaan Elves' name.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I'm sorry. I was in a bad mood.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Apologies accepted.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: That's the first good news I've heard in days. It will make Chun less gloomy, I hope.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: It's not good to be fighting with the Sui Regulator, but I doubt they would be happy to see you get too friendly with your Candleholder.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I understand. But she's really taken to her work, helping me compile the histories... she clearly likes it.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I have a feeling... she didn't become a Candleholder because she wanted to, but because she was alone and didn't have a choice but to take the hand that was offered.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Well, a wrong has been righted. That's always a good thing.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Of course, I think part of their intention is to get you to compromise on changing the documents.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: I simply came to discuss matters, because this matter has gotten to the three Grand Ministers and the True Lung. I'm not lobbying on anybody's behalf.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Just treat it as the guy in the Tomb of Sui throwing a tantrum.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: You're the only one in the family who jokes about this.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Ling has honeyed words, and you speak with heaven's authority. I'll settle for the frivolous tongue, then.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: It's true that the officials of the court are facing a dilemma in this matter.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: The figure of three thousand will cast a shadow upon the nomadic city project, and the implications it may have for Yan are unknown.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Did you tolerate the falsification of records while you were still administering justice?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Falsifying records is a crime, of course. However, if the perpetrator did not do it out of selfish interest, I will consider extenuating circumstances when determining the punishment.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I'm surprised to hear that.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: We each have our own specializations. I don't work in history, and you don't work in law.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Perhaps that is how matters of law work... but not in history.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: I wanted to study history and language because I wanted to learn what the human mind is truly like.

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: The answer to my questions may lie in the intention behind words, and the truth behind history...

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Not for Yan, nor for the land, not even for our family... only for my own questions—

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Jie! Jie!

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Chun? What are you doing here? I wasn't ready to tell you—

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: Tell me what?

steps.name: Jie
steps.text: Never mind... what's the hurry?

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: I went to the study to get the drafts as you asked, but I discovered signs of an intrusion!

steps.name: Chun
steps.text: The writing knife on the desk is gone!
